title: 2 Chronicles 31:11–21
context: To manage the abundance, Hezekiah has storerooms prepared in the LORD’s house, and the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things are brought in faithfully under Conaniah the Levite and his brother Shimei, with named overseers and distributors in the cities of the priests. The portions are given fairly to the great and the small, according to the genealogical registers of priests, Levites, and their households. The chapter closes by saying that Hezekiah did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God, and that in every work he began to seek his God he acted with all his heart and prospered. Arminian and Reformed readers commonly read the passage as shared ground about faithful stewardship, fairness in caring for God’s servants, and wholehearted devotion.

verses.text: Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare rooms in the LORD’s house, and they prepared them.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Hezekiah commanding rooms to be prepared in the LORD’s house for the offerings. Practical planning serves generous giving.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the storerooms as wise stewardship of God’s gifts. Both traditions commonly read the verse as showing that administration matters in God’s service.

verses.text: They brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was ruler over them, and Shimei his brother was second.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the offerings brought in faithfully under Conaniah the Levite and his brother Shimei. Trustworthy leaders manage what is given.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see faithfulness in handling offerings as a mark of godly service. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse as valuing integrity in stewardship.

verses.text: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see named overseers serving under Conaniah and Shimei by the appointment of Hezekiah and Azariah. Shared responsibility ensures accountability.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the careful appointment as reflecting ordered leadership in God’s house. Both traditions commonly read the verse as honoring those who serve behind the scenes.

verses.text: Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the east gate, was over the free will offerings of God, to distribute the LORD’s offerings and the most holy things.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Kore the gatekeeper placed over the freewill offerings and their distribution. Gifts are entrusted to responsible hands.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the distribution of the LORD’s offerings as a sacred trust. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse as showing care for fair distribution.

verses.text: Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in their office of trust, to give to their brothers by divisions, to the great as well as to the small;
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see helpers in the cities of the priests distributing portions to great and small alike. Fairness reaches everyone.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the impartial distribution as reflecting God’s care for all his servants. Both traditions commonly read the verse as a model of justice in sharing resources (compare Acts 4:35).

verses.text: in addition to those who were listed by genealogy of males, from three years old and upward, even everyone who entered into the LORD’s house, as the duty of every day required, for their service in their offices according to their divisions;
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see portions given to males listed by genealogy who entered the LORD’s house for daily service. The record ensures that each receives his share.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the genealogical records as supporting orderly provision. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse as part of a careful system of care.

verses.text: and those who were listed by genealogy of the priests by their fathers’ houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their offices by their divisions;
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see the priests listed by fathers’ houses and the Levites from twenty years old and upward in their divisions. Each has a recognized place.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the registration as maintaining order in service. Both traditions commonly read the verse as continuing the theme of fairness in provision.

verses.text: and those who were listed by genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, through all the congregation; for in their office of trust they sanctified themselves in holiness.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see provision extending to little ones, wives, sons, and daughters, since the servants sanctified themselves in their office of trust. Families are cared for too.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the inclusion of families as showing God’s concern for the households of those who serve. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse as honoring faithful service and its dependents.

verses.text: Also for the sons of Aaron the priests, who were in the fields of the pasture lands of their cities, in every city, there were men who were mentioned by name to give portions to all the males among the priests and to all who were listed by genealogy among the Levites.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see men named to give portions to priests and Levites in the pasture lands of every city. No one is overlooked.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the provision for those outside Jerusalem as thorough and fair. Both traditions commonly read the verse as care reaching the whole priestly community.

verses.text: Hezekiah did so throughout all Judah; and he did that which was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Hezekiah doing what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD throughout Judah. His leadership reflects genuine devotion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the summary as the Chronicler’s high praise of a faithful king. Readers in both traditions commonly read the verse as a model of integrity before God.

verses.text: In every work that he began in the service of God’s house, in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart and prospered.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Hezekiah seeking his God with all his heart in every work and prospering. Wholehearted devotion is honored by God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see his prosperity as God’s blessing on a heart turned toward him, while avoiding the idea that faithfulness guarantees ease. Both traditions commonly read the verse as encouragement to wholehearted service (compare Colossians 3:23).
